findings.title: Unconditional property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`). When `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and the user has no destination calendar configured, this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Co-hosts' destination calendars are dropped when main organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: On lines 1063-1067, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` if neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on a `null` value, so `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded whenever the primary organizer has not set a destinationCalendar, even if collective co-hosts have destination calendars configured. Initializing `destinationCalendar` to `[]` (or assigning `teamDestinationCalendars` when it is null) avoids dropping the co-hosts' calendars.

findings.title: Inverted `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` check sets organization slug before billing completes and breaks self-hosted org creation
findings.body: Line 151 was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. When team billing is enabled, a new organization is supposed to store the slug only in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment succeeds, and when team billing is disabled, the `slug` should be set directly on creation. Inverting this condition causes organizations created when billing is disabled to have `slug: null` (and `requestedSlug` unset), and sets the live `slug` immediately before payment when billing is enabled.

findings.title: `calendar.events.patch` uses `undefined` `calendarId` instead of falling back to `"primary"`
findings.body: On line 147, `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(...)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (previously it defaulted to `"primary"` at assignment). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 was updated to pass `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. If `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`, patching the event description with the Google Meet hangout link will fail because `calendarId` is required by the Google Calendar API.

findings.title: Fallback lookup in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` searches for a falsy `externalCalendarId`
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`). Searching `event.destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch will never match a valid calendar ID and always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, this passes `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update`, causing the Google Calendar API call to fail whenever `externalCalendarId` is not stored on the booking reference.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use `destinationCalendar[0]` instead of matching the current credential
findings.body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each entry in `event.destinationCalendar`. However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (line 128), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (line 156) all read `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` instead of finding the destination calendar matching `credentialId`. In a collective event where the second host uses Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV, their service will use the first host's `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (which may belong to another user or even another integration like Google Calendar), causing event creation for the second host to target the wrong calendar ID or fail.
